newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-RIO CHAMPIONSHIP CHAOS RESUMES AFTER COPA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RIO CHAMPIONSHIP CHAOS RESUMES AFTER COPA.

text.p: Flamengo president Kleber Leite was seething on Wednesday after his team's last two games in the Rio de Janeiro championship were cancelled and the points awarded to their opponents.
Flamengo had been due to play Americano away on Tuesday night and then Vasco da Gama on Thursday to complete the third stage of the chaotic competition.

Leite said that on Monday he had sent a document to the Rio federation requesting a postponment because his team were involved in another tournament and could not play the two games arranged for this week.
But, as the Rio championship chaos resumed after breaking for the Copa America, the federation replied by awarding the two matches to Americano and Vasco by scores of 1-0.

On Tuesday night, Americano's stadium remain locked while Flamengo beat Sao Paulo 1-0 in Brasilia in the so-called "Champions of the World" tournament between Brazilian teams who have won the World Club championship.

The stricken Rio championship had been about to reach its climax in late May when the federation suddenly interrupted the action at the request of Vasco, who had two players picked to play for Brazil in the Copa America which finished on Sunday.

The abrupt halt, which demoralised the other teams involved, came just five days before the final round of games in the third stage were due to be played with the final play-offs immediately afterwards.
Flamengo had an extra game left.

On Monday, the federation also announced that Botafogo's game with Fluminense, the other outstanding third stage game, would be played on Wednesday evening in a small stadium in a distant suburb of Rio.

Vasco's three walkover points virtually guaranteed they would win the third stage and earn a place in the play-offs against Botafogo, who won the first two stages but are out of the running in the third.
Fluminense, who have lost their coach and four key players in transfer moves since the interruption, need to beat Botafogo by a four-goal margin to overhaul Vasco on goals scored.
"We never know when we've got a game coming up," complained Fluminense striker Renato Portaluppi.
Whoever wins the third stage will be at a huge disadvantage against Botafogo in the play-offs in any case.
Under the eccentric format, the first team to six points wins the play-off series but Botafogo have been given a four-point head start by virtue of having won two stages.
"They should just give the title to Botafogo," said Fluminense striker Alcindo. "We want to play but this sort of thing takes away the enjoyment."
The first play-off match is due to be played Saturday but the competition now threatens to clash with the start of the national championship, which is held in the second half of the year.

Vasco are due to play Atletico Mineiro at home on Sunday, with Fluminense away to Palmeiras on Saturday. Fluminense directors, apparently not overconfident in their team's ability to win by four goals on Wednesday, said they had already made the travel arrangements for the Palmeiras game in Sao Paulo.
